newsitem.title: USA: Owens-Illinois to buy Avir of Italy.
newsitem.headline: Owens-Illinois to buy Avir of Italy.

text.p: Owens-Illinois, Inc. said Monday it has a definitive agreement to acquire about 76 percent of Avir S.p.A., the largest manufacturer of glass containers in Italy.
The Toledo, Ohio-based company will also launch a tender offer for the remaining 21 percent of Avir's publicly held shares, bringing the value of the deal to about $580 million.
About one of every two glass containers made worldwide is already manufactured by Owens-Illinois, its affiliates, or its licensees.

The acquisition will make Owens-Illinois the second-largest glass container maker in Europe. It already is the largest in North America, South America, Britain, Poland, Hungary, Finland, Estonia and India.
Avir is the largest glass container manufacturer in the Czech Republic and the fourth largest in Spain. Its major customers are producers of wine, spirits, beer, and food.
The company, based in Milan, Italy, is controlled by Chairman Natale Maderna and members of the Maderna and Ricciardi families.
Owens-Illinois has provided glass-making technology and equipment to Avir for 26 years under a series of technical assistance agreements.
The purchase is expected to boost Owens-Illinois' annual sales by about $600 million and improve earnings in 1997, the company said.

Owens-Illinois said the acquisition will establish its fast-growing global operations as the company's largest business segment, accounting for 40 percent of total sales, up from 28 percent in 1995 and just 18 percent in 1991.
The deal is expected to close in the first quarter of 1997. It will be financed initially by bank borrowings.
Avir is the ninth glass container company Owens-Illinois has acquired since 1991.
Owens-Illinois' stock rose 25 cents to $19.25 on the New York Stock Exchange in late trading.
